title: bug: the guest supervisor's relay leaves a finished job's background processes running and stops watching host EOF once the job closes its output pipes
description: run_bridge stands the guard down on a normal finish without killpg (run_install always kills), so `sleep 300 &` or a setsid child outlives the job until VM deletion, contrary to check-evidence's teardown 'killed-and-reaped'; and pump stops polling in_fd once both output pipes close, so a host EOF (header: exit 74) goes unnoticed while the job runs on. Also: a bridge request pending at job exit turns a real observation into SESSION_PROTOCOL_VIOLATION (guest-session.mjs:169; runAgentJob has no caller yet), and the header's exit 75, materialize's "leaves neither" comment and snapshot-import.mjs's "limit codes surface unchanged" disagree with the code. Changes supervisorSha256, so certification reports must be re-run.
definitionOfDone: After any job ends, no process of its group or session survives the observation frame, and a host EOF is acted on while a job with closed output pipes still runs, with tests.
The supervisor header and the cited comments match the code.

Reuse existing guarded/session/frame helpers, accumulating PID output safely across chunks; assert the actual original exit/signal, one final observation only after owned descendants are gone, bounded completion, and an unrelated sentinel started by the test remains alive. Add a real-Python case whose job closes both output pipes but keeps running: close host in_fd after a deterministic ready/closed-output handshake, expect74 promptly with no observation and owned job cleanup. Add the same quiet-output case with malformed host data expecting76 and keep catchable-signal75 coverage. Existing task-a4a729ddaa8942679e8ae7cd57bd42f1 kernel-boundary tests cover setsid/setpgid/double-fork escape and supervisor SIGKILL; retain those unchanged and exercise its real root-Linux path when validating the completion boundary. Test cleanup may signal only exact recorded PIDs this test started, never names/UIDs/session scans; isolate privileged probes in owned namespaces.

implementationPlan.description: Make guard completion, not stdout/stderr lifetime, drive relay. After startup read returns '+', send the existing life-pipe stand-down byte immediately (as run_install already does); catch BrokenPipeError as the existing self-killed-group case. Extend pump to watch start_end in the SAME Bridge selector alongside host stdin, termination wakeup, agent sockets and output pipes. Keep servicing host EOF/protocol/signals even after both output streams close; no subsequent blocking completion-only read that stops watching host. An EOF on start_end marks guard completion; any unexpected control byte fails closed. Before reaping, SIGKILL the owned original process group while the unreaped guard pins its id (ProcessLookupError is benign), then drain remaining output to EOF. Only when completion EOF and both output EOFs are established may reap supply the single observation. Preserve raw wait status: cleanup must never turn a job's0/7/signal into a different observed result. The prerequisite's root-Linux kernel boundary guarantees all escaped descendants already ended before completion EOF; do not replace it with process scans or broaden kill scope. Keep finally teardown on all errors, close fds/selector/socket exactly once, retain signal-handler/wakeup restoration, and keep error handling mapping71 startup,74 I/O/hostEOF,75 caught signal,76 protocol. No busy polling, extra thread, second selector loop or public frame change.

amendments.reason: Folds governor-693b7073's binding comment-4931235 (from architect-b58e1112, msg-db71184c) into the step text. comments.author: architect-66fd8127
comments.content:
Heads-up from task-a46b60e6, which depends on this row. It is informational only and does not change your plan or DoD.

Under a root runner (`unshare -r`, or real root in a guest), GUARD unshares a PID namespace. Inside the job, os.getpid() and os.getppid() return namespace-local numbers (2 and 1), and so does a fork() return value. A job that calls kill() on the harness's outer pid gets ESRCH. The guest's procfs still reports global pids.

a46b converts the existing rows after you land: S6, AGENT_CHILD, GROUP_JOB, S11, S12, S15, S16, S17, J4, K3, KI1 and KI2. It uses readlink('/proc/self'), /proc/<pid>/stat fields, a fork whose child pipes its global pid to the parent, and harness-side signals. If your NEW rows send job pids to the host (your S11 rewrite, the quiet-output host-EOF case), you may already read them from procfs. Either way, a46b audits and converts whatever remains. Please don't change other rows for this.

Reference: Serena memory task-task-a46b60e6aa63422fbd63934d17238396-prototype.

comments.author: governor-693b7073
comments.content:
Governor plan amendment for step 2 (from architect-b58e1112, msg-db71184c). It is binding for whoever works this row.

Step 2 says "SIGKILL the owned original process group while the unreaped guard pins its id (ProcessLookupError is benign)". Do NOT write a bare `except ProcessLookupError` at that killpg. Catch GROUP_GONE instead.

Why: when the job leaves nothing behind (the usual case), the group holds only the zombie guard. Linux treats the killpg as a no-op, but darwin raises PermissionError. The completion would then fail on macOS, and the macOS CI leg runs the bridge tests. Your WSL gate and QA would not see this.

How:
- If scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py already defines GROUP_GONE (the CI fix for PR #230, branch fix/ci-pr230, is due to land on this branch soon), reuse it: `except GROUP_GONE:`.
- If it does not exist yet, add this exact definition after pump(), with its comment, so the later merge sees an identical line on both sides:
```
# killpg errors that mean no member of the job group is left to kill: ESRCH, and on darwin, where only the tests run this
# file, EPERM for a group of zombies (Linux signals one as a no-op).
GROUP_GONE = (ProcessLookupError, PermissionError) if sys.platform == 'darwin' else ProcessLookupError
```
Check: after your change, `grep -c "except ProcessLookupError" scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py` must print 0.

QA review of round-2 completion c96c587b (qa-4398294e, 2026-10-31): APPROVE. All four reopen-1 points are closed.

**Delivery**
- c96c587b (tree 30620db1) is a completion commit on moe/work-2026-10-24 and on origin. It was recorded at 15:26:58Z, after the reject at 14:40:03Z.
- Owned-file diff: supervisor +10/-7 (header comment only), bridge test +48/-1. With b245f476, the task totals +273/-60 on the two files, under 400.
- sha256 at c96c587b: supervisor 3a19f3bf…8190, test 98c56dc8…39ea. Both match the worker's gate overlays and the CQ-R13 hand-off (comment-b187a175 on task-f4811a72).

**Gate, fresh**
- Snapshot: full `git archive c96c587b` at /tmp/qa97341r2-gate-EoI8nH. npm ci + build ran only in its packages/moe-daemon; the lockfile 3257552d… is unchanged.
  - Prebuild rewrote src/generated/initFiles.ts's historical-hash list. That happens in any archive with no .git, and the earlier gates share it.
- Environment: env -i, Node 24.21.0, npm 12.2.0, Python 3.12.3, WSL2 6.18.33.1, uid 1000.
- The exact task.verification command:
  - node --test: 648 tests, 645 pass, 0 fail, 3 skips (LA5, K9, macOS smoke).
  - vitest: 215/215 files, 6341 passed, 20 skipped.
  - GATE_EXIT=0. Ran 15:32:20Z–15:34:35Z; 1-min load went from 8.9 to 14.3. No leftover processes carried my env marker.

**DoD 2: header vs code (every return, per mode)**
- 71:
  - start_job: no account, home or config, before relay, no frame.
  - materialize: KeyError from getpwnam(AGENT_IDENTITY) gives EX_OSERR, reachable from main(['materialize']). It is now named.
  - export: drop() gives 71.
  - run_bridge's first try: the wake_r register, bridge.open (in_fd, socket, KeyError) and the guard Popen give 71 before any child exists.
  - No '+': 71, and the finally killpg's the group.
- 74/75/76 after hello all come after Popen. The finally kills the group, or pump's start-EOF killpg already has, before a failed observation write.
- Other paths:
  - A failed hello write gives 74 with no job.
  - read_job EOFError/OSError gives 74.
  - codex .codex gives 65; 66 is the workspace; 64 and 77 come from main.
  - relay() returns 0 only after write_frame(observation).
  - PR #232's loads() ValueError stays in the 65/76 buckets.
- The GUARD, pump, materialize, run_install and EX_TERMINATED comments are unchanged since round 1. Added lines are ≤120 columns and ASCII. GROUP_GONE is identical to a4c8204d, `except ProcessLookupError` count is 0, and ast parses.

**S20 drain rows: my own driver**
- /tmp/qa97341r2/tools/mut.py with m-drain.json, pattern `^S(1[1-9]|20) `, 4 in parallel. The control passes 18/18.
- KILLED:
  - M04: loop only on start_end.
  - M04b: return after the start-EOF killpg.
  - Stdout-only drain and stderr-only drain: each fails the other stream's row.
  - Outputs unregistered at start EOF.
  - The pre-task outputs-only loop: S11-closed, S15, S17 and S18 fail.
- M04 and M04b pass the held [true] precondition, then fail on `relayed <stream> bytes expected 524288 actual 131072`.
- S20 passed 16/16 in 4-parallel repeats.

**Other checks**
- OBSERVE ESRCH: a probe (open /proc/<pid>/status, reap, then read) raises ProcessLookupError errno 3. done() now counts it as reaped.
- `unshare -r`, S11–S20: 16/18 pass. S12 and S16 fail the same way on pre-task b6cfcc4e (task-a46b60e6's rows). Every S11/S18/S19/S20 row passes.
- Windows (Node 24.16 via cmd.exe, temp copy since removed): 76 tests, 23 pass, 0 fail, 53 skipped. S20 skips with the NO_GUEST reason.

**Non-blocking**
1. Pre-existing and disclosed: an EMFILE from Bridge() or the life/start os.pipe() between hello and run_bridge's try exits 1 uncaught. b6cfcc4e has the same order.
2. S20 needs unprivileged F_SETPIPE_SZ up to 1 MiB, the default pipe-max-size. On a host with a lower cap the row fails loudly; it does not pass vacuously.

No certification or verified-local claim is made. CQ-R13 owns native re-certification of 3a19f3bf….

completionSummary: Reopen-1 fix for QA comment-b4b7df23 (DoD 2) and governor comment-692404a2; all four points closed. (1a) The exit-code header names materialize's no-AGENT_IDENTITY-account 71 again. (1b) It claims the child-group kill only where a group started: a 71 for a failed bridge setup (wakeup pipe, host stream, agent socket) or a guard that could not start comes before any child exists; a 71 for a guard that could not start the job, and 74/75/76, kill the group. It also names relay()'s hello-write 74, the bridge's pre-job-frame 74 and codex .codex 65. The supervisor change is comment-only, and GROUP_GONE is byte-identical to PR #232. (2) S20 stdout+stderr: the job sets F_SETPIPE_SZ to 1 MiB, writes 512 KiB and exits 3; the harness holds the first output frame until waitid(WNOWAIT) shows the guard exited (asserted; at least 448 KiB unread). Each row asserts the exact 524288 bytes, the other stream empty, the observation as the last frame and exit code 3. (3) OBSERVE done() treats ProcessLookupError (ESRCH) as reaped. Mutants on the final bytes (^S(1[1-9]|20)): the control passed 18/18; M04 and M04b were killed (131072 bytes relayed instead of 524288), as were the stdout-only and stderr-only drains; 0 leftover pids. Mid-task, the main merge c9b771ea (PR #232) re-applied my uncommitted edits; a diff-of-diffs shows identical change lines, and the header still holds (loads() ValueError falls in the existing 65/76 buckets). Gate on HEAD e8df3882 plus the 2 overlays, npm ci/build in the snapshot only, env -i Node 24.21.0: node --test 648 tests, 645 pass, 0 fail, 3 skips (LA5, K9, macOS smoke); vitest 215 files, 6341 passed, 20 skipped; GATE_EXIT=0. The new supervisorSha256 3a19f3bf07cf6d47a1fb93e425b4bf7f1eb7e2b3b2d31bb21ba00752ecef8190 went to CQ-R13 as comment-b187a175, superseding 494b6ad6 and 873e7ccb. No certification is claimed; verified-local stays unavailable. Pre-existing theoretical residual: EMFILE before run_bridge's try exits 1 after hello, no child.

failedDodItems: The supervisor header and the cited comments match the code.

issues.description: DoD 2 (header lines 12-13): '71 the job could not start, or the export could not become the AGENT_IDENTITY account' drops materialize's 71. materialize() returns EX_OSERR on KeyError from pwd.getpwnam(AGENT_IDENTITY) (lines 667-672), which main()'s ['materialize'] reaches. CQ-R09c (efffad66) documented it, and the pre-task header still had it. To pass: name materialize's no-account 71 again.

DoD 2 (lines 16-17): the text says every after-hello 71, including 'the guard ... or the agent socket could not start', kills the child group. A failed guard Popen or bridge.open returns 71 from run_bridge's `except (OSError, KeyError)` (line 504) before any child exists. To pass: claim the kill only where a child group started. Then re-hash, re-gate and hand the new supervisorSha256 to CQ-R13 (task-f4811a72), superseding comment-873e7ccb.

Plan step 2 needs both output EOFs before the observation; nothing pins it. M04 (line 436 becomes `while start_end in selector.get_map():`) and M04b (`return` after the start-EOF killpg) survive every bridge, check and guard row. Probe /tmp/qa97341-tools/drain_probe.py (1 MiB stdout pipe, 512 KiB written, 0.1 s per output frame): correct code relays 524288 bytes, the mutants 131072, then exit 3. To pass: a row (Linux-only is fine) that kills both and asserts the exact bytes and the job status.

Minor: OBSERVE's done() counts only FileNotFoundError as reaped. A pid released between open('/proc/<pid>/status') and the first read raises ProcessLookupError (ESRCH). That escapes the write_frame hook, run_bridge's `except OSError` returns 74 with no observation, and an S11 row fails spuriously. Treat ProcessLookupError as reaped too.

rejectionHistory.reason:
DoD 2 fails: the rewritten exit-code header no longer matches the code. Also, the start-EOF drain path this task added has no test; removing it drops output silently.

What holds (full evidence in comment-b4b7df23):
- Fresh snapshot gate of b245f476: node --test 645 tests, 642 pass, 0 fail, 3 pre-existing skips; vitest 215/215 files, 6341 pass; GATE_EXIT=0.
- RED: on the parent supervisor, 9 of 16 S11-S19 rows fail.
- Root-runner S11/S18/S19 pass.
- 6 independent mutants are killed.
- GROUP_GONE matches a4c8204d.
- Code review: completion order and teardown are correct.

Required fixes:
1. Header (DoD 2):
   - Lines 12-13 dropped materialize's 71 for a missing AGENT_IDENTITY account (lines 667-672, reachable from main). CQ-R09c (efffad66) had documented it.
   - Lines 16-17 say every after-hello 71 kills the child group. But a failed guard Popen or agent socket returns 71 before any child exists (line 504).
2. Drain test: no row pins "both output EOFs before the observation".
   - Two mutants survive every bridge, check and guard row:
     - M04: the line-436 loop becomes `while start_end in selector.get_map():`.
     - M04b: `return` right after the start-EOF killpg.
   - With a job that enlarges its stdout pipe and a slow host consumer, both mutants relay 128 of 512 KiB, then write a normal exit observation. That is silent data loss.
   - Add a row that kills both mutants.
3. Minor: OBSERVE's done() should treat ProcessLookupError (ESRCH) as reaped.

After the fixes, re-run the full snapshot gate and hand the new supervisorSha256 to CQ-R13.

reviewSummary:
APPROVED round 2, completion c96c587b (on moe/work-2026-10-24 and origin, recorded after the reject). Full evidence: comment-27d25f5c.

Size: owned diff supervisor +10/-7 (header comment only) and bridge test +48/-1. With b245f476 the task totals +273/-60, under 400.

Gate, fresh: full git archive of c96c587b; npm ci + build ran only in the snapshot (lockfile unchanged); env -i Node 24.21.0, Python 3.12.3, WSL2 uid 1000; the exact task.verification command.
- node --test: 648 tests, 645 pass, 0 fail, 3 skips (LA5, K9, macOS smoke).
- vitest: 215/215 files, 6341 passed.
- GATE_EXIT=0; wall-clock 2m15s; no leftover processes.

DoD 1: S11 x6, S18 x3 and S19 pass in the gate. Runtime is unchanged since round-1 QA verified it.

DoD 2: I audited every return per mode. Materialize's no-account 71 is named again. The no-child 71s (wake_r register, bridge.open, guard Popen) are separated from the no-'+' 71 and from 74/75/76, which kill the group. Hello-write 74, read_job 74, codex .codex 65, and "returns 0 only once the observation is written" all match the code, and PR #232's loads() errors stay in the 65/76 buckets. Lines are 120 columns or less and ASCII; GROUP_GONE is identical to a4c8204d.

S20, my own mutation driver over S11-S20: the control passes 18/18. Killed: M04, M04b (131072 of 524288 bytes relayed), stdout-only and stderr-only drains, outputs unregistered at start EOF, and the pre-task loop. S20 passed 16/16 parallel repeats.

OBSERVE: the ESRCH premise is confirmed by a probe.

Other runs:
- unshare -r: every S11/S18/S19/S20 row passes; S12/S16 fail the same way on pre-task b6cfcc4e (owned by task-a46b60e6).
- Windows Node 24.16: 0 fail; S20 skips via NO_GUEST.

The supervisorSha256 3a19f3bf... reached CQ-R13 (comment-b187a175). No certification is claimed.

Non-blocking: a pre-existing EMFILE between hello and the try exits 1 (disclosed). S20 assumes F_SETPIPE_SZ can reach 1 MiB; if it can't, the row fails loudly.
